title: Hierarchical Clustering
subtitle: Agglomerative Merging & Dendrogram Cut-off
summary: Build a bottom-up merge hierarchy and slice the Dendrogram at any linkage distance.

evaluationChart.title: Agglomerative Linkage Dendrogram
evaluationChart.description: Visualizes the hierarchical merge tree; horizontal dashed line indicates the active distance cut-off.

advantages: Produces a complete multi-scale hierarchy (Dendrogram) without fixing K beforehand.
Deterministic output with no random centroid initialization.
Supports custom distance metrics and linkage criteria.
limitations: O(n²) to O(n³) time and O(n²) memory — unsuitable for massive datasets.
Greedy merge decisions cannot be undone in later steps.
Sensitive to noise and chaining effects under single linkage.

formulas.label: Average Linkage Distance
formulas.description: Measures mean pairwise Euclidean distance between two candidate clusters.

hyperparameters.label: Dendrogram Cut-off
hyperparameters.description: Distance threshold slicing the Dendrogram into discrete clusters.

codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1.5,2.0],[2.1,2.4],[5.8,6.4],[6.4,6.9],[7.5,2.2],[8.1,2.7]])
agg = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=None, distance_threshold=2.5, linkage='average')
print('Labels:', agg.fit_predict(X))
